fact_check_verdict: PASS. Publish as a funded plan, future tense. No results, no named Alaska coal source, no lead institution named.

claims.spoken: On October fifth, UAF announced it is joining a six million dollar National Science Foundation project.
requires: UAF is JOINING, not leading. Say joining. $6M is a rounded figure of three awards totaling $5,998,412.
claims.verbatim: UAF researchers at the Institute of Northern Engineering are joining a $6 million National Science Foundation-funded project

claims.spoken: The partners are UAF, UAA, Montana Tech, and the University of Wyoming.
requires: Never name a lead institution. Neither source says who leads.

claims.spoken: UAF's share is about nine hundred thirteen thousand dollars.
requires: Exact NSF figure $913,037; UAF says nearly $913,000. Use ABOUT $913,000 spoken.

claims.spoken: The plan is to use microbes to recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash.
requires: Research plan only. Verb is studies how it CAN recover. Name no Alaska coal source or mine.
claims.verbatim: recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash

claims.spoken: AI will predict how readily rare earths can be recovered from different materials.
requires: Future tense. Do not say AI predicts as if it already does.
claims.verbatim: predicting how readily rare earth elements can be recovered from different materials

claims.spoken: A second AI effort will adjust the bioreactor as conditions and available energy change.
requires: Future tense, planned work.
claims.verbatim: adjust bioreactor operation as conditions and energy availability change

claims.spoken: The team calls the goal a smart bio-refinery, tested first as a virtual pilot plant.
requires: A virtual pilot plant is computer models, not a physical plant. The bio-refinery is a goal.
claims.verbatim: A virtual pilot plant will connect experimental results with computer models

claims.spoken: The award runs from September 2026 through August 2030.
No results have been reported yet.
requires: Both sources describe planned work only.

claims.spoken: Lab and small-scale pilot tests will refine the models, and the team will evaluate costs, energy needs and environmental impacts.
claims.on_screen: COST · ENERGY · ENVIRONMENT TO BE EVALUATED
requires: Future tense.

claims.spoken: Srijan Aggarwal, who leads UAF's part, says Alaska's remote energy challenges make energy use a central part of the question.
requires: Quote needs context: the question is keeping biological processes working reliably.
claims.verbatim: Alaska's remote energy challenges make energy use a central part of that question.

claims.spoken: UAF says it is one of eight projects sharing thirty nine point nine million dollars across sixteen jurisdictions.
requires: Attribute to UAF only; not verified at NSF.

claims.spoken: Rare earth atoms can cling to a cell's outer wall. The microbe doesn't eat them.
claims.source: general biosorption science; NSF abstract names Shewanella oneidensis extraction (https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2614749.json)
requires: General mechanism, labelled illustrative. Not a result of this project. The project's own organism or method is not specified beyond the NSF abstract.

claims.spoken: Ship the ash where power is cheap.
claims.source: film's own framing of the fair counterpoint (angle.json)
requires: Frame as the alternative the plan has to beat. No cost figure, no claim that it is cheaper, no named place.

claims.spoken: Here's the honest read. Energy isn't an afterthought in this plan. It's the design brief.
requires: Label as the channel's read. Falsifiable by the 2030 results.

claims.spoken: Fairbanks professor Srijan Aggarwal
claims.on_screen: SRIJAN AGGARWAL · UAF PROFESSOR OF ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING
requires: Aggarwal is a UAF professor of environmental engineering and leads UAF's work.

claims.spoken: Two A I tools are planned.
requires: Planned work. NSF abstract and UAF release describe two AI efforts.

claims.spoken: Living cells stall when power does.
claims.source: argument from the NSF abstract's premise that biological processes must be kept working reliably (c11 context)
requires: Illustrative cutaway. Not a measured result. Planned work only.

claims.spoken: Power is the risk, so they'll build the plant in software first, a virtual pilot plant.
claims.source: UAF release (c7); the 'so' is the channel's inference
requires: The virtual pilot plant is computer models. The causal 'so' is our reading, not the source's.

claims.spoken: A smart controller can adapt to expensive power. It can't make power cheaper.
claims.on_screen: IT ADAPTS · CAN'T MAKE POWER CHEAPER
requires: Draw every working-controller image as planned (dashed, PLANNED). The price tag carries no number.
